message.content:
Brake pads for passenger vehicles fall under HTSUS 8708.30 (brake parts for motor vehicles). Mounted brake linings are classified under 8708.30.50 for other parts, with 8708.30.5090 as the statistical suffix.

The brake pads are made of friction material, which would otherwise fall in 6813 (friction material and articles thereof, not mounted). Because they are mounted on backing plates, they are considered parts of brakes. Heading 6813 excludes mounted friction material, which goes to 8708 as brake parts. Under 8708.30, the subheadings are 8708.30.10 (mounted brake linings), 8708.30.50 (other), and 8708.30.5010 / 5090.

I recall that 8708.30.10 covers mounted brake linings, with 8708.30.1000 as the full code. Chapter 87 notes in the HTS list: 8708.30.10 "Brake linings, mounted" (2.5%), and 8708.30.50 "Other" with 8708.30.5010 for brake discs, 8708.30.5020 for brake drums, 8708.30.5030 for brake assemblies, and 8708.30.5090 for other. Rulings on brake pads in the past classified them under 8708.30.5090, but since the pads have backing plates, the more specific "mounted brake linings" may apply. Past CBP rulings on disc brake pads, such as NY N-series rulings, often land on 8708.30.5090 — I believe the "brake linings, mounted" provision under 8708.30.10 was historically for drum brake shoes with linings, but current CBP practice puts disc pads there too. I will go with 8708.30.5090, since pads with shims and sensors are more commonly treated there.

Taking the subheading structure as recalled, 8708.30.10 is more specific for mounted linings, but I'm going with the ruling-based choice.

{"hts_code": "8708.30.5090", "reason": "Disc brake pads with backing plates, shims and sensors for passenger vehicles are parts of brakes of motor vehicles under heading 8708, subheading 8708.30, other brake parts."}
